Dear Colleague,

Reason for referral: Evaluation of recurrent palpitations in an 80-year-old man with atrial fibrillation.

I am referring Kenneth Grant, an 80-year-old man with atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes, for evaluation of recurrent palpitations.

He describes intermittent fluttering sensations over the past several weeks, lasting a few minutes at a time. He denies dizziness, fainting, or chest discomfort during these episodes. Please assess and advise on further care.

William Morris, MD, Brookside Family Practice

Thank you for seeing this patient.

Dr. William Morris

SUBJECTIVE:
Kenneth Grant is an 80-year-old man with atrial fibrillation who reports intermittent fluttering sensations over the past several weeks, lasting a few minutes at a time. He denies dizziness, fainting, or chest discomfort during these episodes.

VITALS:
BP 137/85, HR 72, RR 15, SpO2 95% on room air, weight 153 lb.

EXAM:
General: well appearing, no distress.
Neck: no carotid bruits.
Cardiac exam: regular rate and rhythm, normal S1 and S2, soft systolic murmur at the sternal border, no gallop.
Lungs: faint bibasilar crackles.
Extremities: trace ankle edema.

DATA REVIEWED:

Most recent echo showed an ejection fraction of 30%.

Patient is on warfarin.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
1. Recurrent palpitations in the setting of atrial fibrillation. Arrange cardiology evaluation.
2. Atrial fibrillation. Continue ongoing management and review symptoms at follow-up.
3. Hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Continue routine follow-up for both conditions.
